[Writing R Packages]{.custom-title}

[Grayson White]{.custom-subtitle} [Math 241
Week 11 \| Spring 2026]{.custom-subtitle} ::: ::::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Announcements ::: {.nonincremental} * Fill out [this form](https://forms.gle/6FBbcMFmbSpyEeHM7) ASAP to help me create the Project 2 groups. + Groups and project instructions will be assigned on Monday. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Week 11 Goals :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .nonincremental} **Monday Lecture**: - Practice with local LLMs ::: ::: {.column .fragment .nonincremental} **Wednesday Lecture**: - Intro to writing `R` packages ::: :::: # Sharing Code ::: {.fragment} **How do you share code?** ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Sharing Code ### Options: ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * `R` scripts and Quarto documents * RStudio Projects * GitHub Repository * R Package :::
::: {.fragment} **How to pick between the options?** ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## When To Create an `R` Package * If you have certain recurring operations that occur across multiple projects. * Want to share data and documentation and not worry about file paths, file types, the documentation getting lost... * **BUT**, you will still use an RStudio Project (with a corresponding GitHub repo) for the code and data that are specific to a given project. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## R Packages What is an `R` package? ::: {.fragment} > "R packages are the fundamental unit of R-ness". -- Jenny Bryan ::: ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Contains (usually) functions, (possibly) datasets, documentation, and tests. * "base R": a handful of base packages that are preloaded. * CRAN has > 23,000 more packages + `install.packages("dplyr")` + `library(dplyr)` * And then there are all the packages on `GitHub`: + `devtools::install_github("hadley/genzplyr")` + `library(genzplyr)` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### R Data Packages * Great way to share data! ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Example 1: + `library(mosaicData)` + `data(package = "mosaicData")` + `?Births2015` ::: ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Example 2: + `library(pdxTrees)` + `get_pdxTrees_parks()` + `get_pdxTrees_streets()` ::: ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Example 3: + `library(gbfs)` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### R Packages #### Why create an R package? ::: {.fragment .nonincremental} * Very portable. * Includes documentation. * Provides a useful structure for organizing your work: + `R` folder: Code + `tests` folder: Testing functions + `data` folder: Storing data * Lots of helper functions in other packages to automate parts of the process. ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Creating an R Package Key packages: * [`devtools`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/devtools/index.html): supports the development and dissemination of the package * [`usethis`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/): automates steps of package creation, such as constructing the data file * [`roxygen2`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/roxygen2/vignettes/roxygen2.html): simplifies writing documentation ------------------------------------------------------------------------ # Let's Build an `R` Package! ------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Our Package: `usaForests` **Goals**: * Share data on forest attributes across the United States, along with documentation about how the data were collected. * Create a function that outputs a spatial plot of forest attributes for a chosen region. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Our Package: `usaForests`. Useful MVP code: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(sf) resp <- read_rds("data/conus_resp_pltcn.rds") aux <- read_rds("data/conus_aux_pltcn.rds") ecomap <- read_rds("data/ecomap.rds") naTo0 <- function(x) { ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x) } usaForests <- left_join(aux, resp, by = "PLT_CN") %>% mutate(across(colnames(resp)[-1], naTo0)) map_forest_attr <- function(data, x, province){ data <- data %>% filter(PROVINCE %in% province) %>% group_by(SUBSECTION) %>% summarize(avg = mean( {{x}} )) %>% left_join(ecomap, by = "SUBSECTION") %>% st_as_sf() p <- ggplot(data) + geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = avg)) + scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + theme_bw() return(p) } ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ #### Our Package: `usaForests`. Useful MVP code: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='column-fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code} map_forest_attr <- function(data, x, province){ data <- data %>% filter(PROVINCE %in% province) %>% group_by(SUBSECTION) %>% summarize(avg = mean( {{x}} )) %>% left_join(ecomap, by = "SUBSECTION") %>% st_as_sf() p <- ggplot(data) + geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = avg)) + scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greens", direction = 1) + theme_bw() return(p) } map_forest_attr(usaForests, DRYBIO_AG_TON_TPA_ADJ_live, "M333") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](math241_wk11wed_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Steps * Let's go through the "Creating an R Package" hand-out. * I will demo the process with data from the US Forest Service, FIA program. * If following along, clone this repo: [https://github.com/Reed-Data-Science/pkgDemo](https://github.com/Reed-Data-Science/pkgDemo) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Wrap-Up Thought: Most common confusions when moving from **`R` scripts/Quarto docs** to **writing `R` packages**: ::: {.nonincremental .fragment} * Requires new ways of working with functions in other packages. * `DESCRIPTION` file to declare dependencies. * Use `package_name::function_name()`. * Can't use `library(package_name)`. * Want to avoid unnecessary dependencies. :::
::: {.fragment} **Other questions?** ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### Next week ::: {.nonincremental} - More writing `R` packages! :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
